newsitem.title: LEBANON: Police flood central Beirut area before protest.
newsitem.headline: Police flood central Beirut area before protest.

text.p: Hundreds of armed police took up positions in the area of the Lebanese prime minister's office in Beirut on Wednesday, hours before a planned protest sit-in called by media workers and labour unions outside the building.
The protest is to demand the repeal of a law slashing the number of private televison and radio stations and awarding a handful of licences to stations belonging to prominent establishment figures.
There have been widespread accusations that the government is trying to muzzle the media while carving up lucrative franchises for the benefit of its members and their supporters.

Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, a billionaire who owns one of the four licenced TV stations and one of the 11 radios, has slapped a ban on public demonstrations since 1993 -- the first permanent ban on protests in Lebanon's history.
Police with automatic rifles deployed around Hariri's office as the cabinet held an unusual morning session to avoid the sit-in planned for late afternoon.

Police prevented a similar protest last week but anger against the new law has grown with protests by Lebanon's Christians against the proposed closure of a religious television station and two religious radios.
Hundreds of media workers, opposition politicians and unionists defied the ban last Thursday and briefly marched in Beirut after police stopped them staging a sit-in.
The media law is expected to put 3,000 media workers out of work.
